footerHonest.message: Circumvention, not anonymity. No tool is unblockable; OpenRoute stacks fallbacks so something usually gets through.

bannerNeedsHostAccess.message: OpenRoute needs access to all sites to route the blocked ones. It never reads page content.

bannerOtherExtension.message: Another extension controls the proxy settings, so OpenRoute can't route. Turn off the other proxy or VPN extension.

bannerNoProxyApi.message: This browser has no proxy API. OpenRoute can diagnose blocks and suggest fixes, but can't route sites.

bannerPolicyLocked.message: A policy on this device locks the proxy settings, so OpenRoute can't route.

statusExhausted.description: Site status: every transport failed; retried later.

statusManual.description: Site status: the user chose its route.

exhaustedAllFailed.message: Every transport failed for this site.

rungDoh.description: Route: the browser's DNS over HTTPS.

rungEch.description: Route: Secure DNS with Encrypted Client Hello.

rungFallback.description: Route: Wayback or reader copy of the page.

typeSniDpi.description: Diagnosis: filtering by the site name in the TLS handshake.

typeIpBlock.description: Diagnosis: the server's IP address is blocked.

remedyDnsTampering.message: Your DNS resolver is faking answers. Secure DNS fixes this at full speed; until then OpenRoute routes the site.

remedyDnsNxdomain.message: Encrypted DNS says this domain doesn't exist; check the address. A read-only copy may still work.

remedyDnsUnverified.message: DNS failed and encrypted DNS is unreachable too, likely deeper DNS blocking. OpenRoute routes it; the transport looks names up.

remedyDohTampered.message: Even encrypted DNS returned a fake or private address. OpenRoute routes around it.

remedySniDpi.message: The connection was reset during the TLS handshake: filtering by site name (SNI / DPI). ECH, DPI bypass or a tunnel defeats it.

remedyTlsMitm.message: The certificate was invalid: something is intercepting the connection, often to show a block page. OpenRoute routes it.

remedyIpBlock.message: DNS is fine, but traffic to the server is dropped. It needs a proxy or tunnel; OpenRoute routes it.

remedyUnreachable.message: The server didn't answer and DNS couldn't be checked. It may be down, or blocked by address.

remedyPolicyBlock.message: Blocked by a policy or firewall on this device or network, not by your ISP.

remedyDnsBlockpage.message: The page loaded, but from an address your resolver made up: a block page. Secure DNS fixes it at full speed; OpenRoute routes it meanwhile.

remedyHttp451.message: The server, or a filter in between, answered 451 Unavailable For Legal Reasons. OpenRoute routes it through another country.

remedyUnknown.message: Couldn't tell how it's blocked. OpenRoute will try routing it.

navLabel.description: Screen-reader heading of the dashboard navigation.

sitesLead.message: Sites that failed to load, grouped by the domain OpenRoute routes. Open one for its diagnosis, history and controls.

confirmClearAll.message: Forget every site and its route? OpenRoute starts over and detects blocks again as you browse.

sitesEmptyDashboard.message: Nothing here yet. Sites appear when they fail to load.

routeFor.description: Screen-reader label of a route picker.

routeVia.description: Route option; {via} is a transport name.

forget.description: Button: remove the site and its route.

wayback.description: Button: open the Internet Archive copy.

history.description: Heading of a site's event list.

transportsLead.message: Where OpenRoute sends blocked sites: proxies you run, the companion's tunnels, or Tor. Each is tested before it carries a site.

confirmRemoveTransport.message: Remove {name}? Sites using it move to another transport.

proxyLoginHint.message: Chromium browsers can log in to HTTP(S) proxies only; for a SOCKS proxy with a login, use the companion.

addedNotReachable.message: Added, but it didn't answer yet. Check that it's running.

companionUnsupportedHelp.message: This browser can't talk to apps on your computer. Use a proxy you already run, or Tor.

companionHelp.message: The companion runs tunnels a browser can't: your own server, DPI bypass and Tor.

companionInstallHelp.message: Install the companion to use your own server, DPI bypass and Tor. Setup: companion/README.md in OpenRoute's repository.

companionServerHelp.message: Paste share links, one per line: Shadowsocks, VLESS-Reality, VMess, Trojan, Hysteria2, TUIC, WireGuard, or a subscription. Several links become a pool that fails over by itself.

dpiHelp.message: Splits the TLS handshake so simple filters can't read the site's name. Free and fast, but sophisticated censors aren't fooled; OpenRoute moves on to a tunnel when it doesn't work.

torHelp.message: The free network: slower, but it works where your own server's address is blocked. Bridges hide that you use Tor.

torBridgesPlaceholder.message: Bridge lines from bridges.torproject.org, one per line

torStarting.message: Tor ({mode}) is starting; connecting can take a minute.

torNewIdentityDone.message: New connections get new Tor circuits.

dnsLead.message: How OpenRoute checks a failing site's DNS, and how to fix DNS blocking at the source.

secureDnsHelp.message: DNS tampering is the most common block, and your browser's own Secure DNS (DNS over HTTPS) fixes it at full speed for every site. Turn it on once.

remoteDiagnosis.message: Check failing sites with encrypted DNS

remoteDiagnosisHint.message: Sends only the failing site's domain to the resolver below, to tell DNS tampering from other blocks.

consentNeeded.message: Firefox needs your consent for this.

customDohHint.message: An RFC 8484 endpoint, for example your own server. It's tried first; the built-in resolvers stay as fallbacks.

rulesLead.message: Rules override automatic decisions. A rule covers the domain and everything under it.

rulesAlwaysHelp.message: Sent through your best transport even when it would load directly.

rulesNeverHelp.message: Always loads directly; OpenRoute won't diagnose or route it.

routeScope.message: What to route when a site is blocked

routeScopeRegistrable.message: The whole site (example.co.uk and its subdomains)

routeScopeHost.message: Only the exact host that failed

bundles.message: Route a site's own CDNs with it

bundlesHint.message: For example twimg.com with x.com, so pages don't half-load.

autoRouteHint.message: When off, OpenRoute only diagnoses and you route sites yourself.

autoReload.message: Reload the page after routing it

autoReloadHint.message: At most a few times per site, never in a loop.

detectionEnabled.message: Notice sites that fail to load

detectionEnabledHint.message: The heart of OpenRoute: without it, only your rules apply.

deepDetectionHint.message: Also catches block pages, HTTP 451 and a routed site's blocked resources. Needs access to all sites in Chromium browsers.

deepNeedsAccess.message: Deep detection needs access to all sites.

webrtcProtection.message: Keep WebRTC from bypassing the proxy

webrtcProtectionHint.message: Stops calls and peer-to-peer traffic from going around a routed site with your real address. Can break some calls.

webrtcNeedsPermission.message: WebRTC protection needs the browser's privacy permission.

webrtcNotApplied.message: Couldn't apply it: the privacy permission is missing.

backupHelp.message: Your settings, rules and own transports, as a file. Sites and history aren't included.

resetHelp.message: Forget every site, rule, setting and your own transports. The companion's tunnels and the Tor presets stay.

confirmReset.message: Reset OpenRoute to a fresh install? This can't be undone.

reportHelp.message: Downloads what OpenRoute saw and decided, to attach to a bug report. Proxy addresses and passwords are never included.

eventDemoted.message: {domain} works directly again, so its route was removed.

eventBundle.description: Timeline. {added} is a list of domains.

eventDiscovery.message: Looked for local proxies on {tested} ports: found {found}.

eventDohViaTransport.message: Encrypted DNS is blocked here; reaching it through {via}.

welcomeSub.message: Finds out what's blocking a site, then routes only that site around it, at full speed.

onbPermsHelp.message: Your browser asks you before an extension can do these. OpenRoute never reads page content.

onbHostHelp.message: — needed to route the blocked ones through a proxy.

onbConsentHelp.message: — when a site fails, its domain is checked with an encrypted DNS resolver to tell DNS tampering from other blocks. Routing works without it.

onbPrivateHelp.message: — to route there too, open about:addons → OpenRoute → Run in Private Windows → Allow.

onbStep1Text.message: DNS tampering is the most common block, and Secure DNS is the zero-latency fix. It takes one toggle in {browser}.
onbStep1Text.description: {browser} is a browser name, or “your browser”.

yourBrowser.description: Used when the browser's name is unknown.

onbStep2Text.message: When a site fails to load, OpenRoute diagnoses how it's blocked and walks it down a ladder of fixes automatically:

onbLadderDns.message: — beats DNS tampering at full speed

onbLadderEch.message: — hides which site you visit, where the site supports it

onbLadderDpi.message: — splits the handshake so simple filters can't read it (companion app)

onbLadderProxy.message: — routes address-blocked sites through a transport you add

onbLadderTor.message: — the free fallback when even your server is blocked

onbLadderReadOnly.message: — a Wayback or reader copy, so you can still read the page

onbOnlyBlocked.message: Only blocked sites detour. Everything else stays direct and full-speed.

onbStep3Title.message: Beat address blocks and DPI: add a transport

onbStep3Text.message: For sites blocked by address, OpenRoute needs somewhere unblocked to route through: a proxy or Tor you already run, or your own server through the companion app.

onbCompanionUnsupported.message: This browser can't talk to the companion app; use a proxy or Tor you already run.

onbCompanionFound.message: Companion found: connect your server, DPI bypass or Tor in the dashboard.

onbCompanionMissing.message: The companion app isn't installed (it's optional). Setup: companion/README.md and server/README.md in OpenRoute's repository.

onbHonestText.message: No tool is unblockable. OpenRoute stacks independent fixes so that, in practice, something usually gets through. It's circumvention, not anonymity: for anonymity, use Tor Browser. Know your local laws.

onbReopen.message: Everything is in the dashboard, behind the OpenRoute button.
